candidates.topic: The Man Who Never Slept — Fatal Familial Insomnia
candidates.teaser: A disease exists that forces you to stay awake until you die — and there is no cure.
candidates.video_title: The Disease That Literally Won't Let You Sleep
candidates.video_description: Fatal Familial Insomnia is a prion disease that strips the brain of the ability to sleep, leading to hallucinations, organ failure, and death within months. Only around 100 families worldwide carry the gene. There is no treatment.
candidates.script: There is a disease that makes it physically impossible to sleep — and once it starts, you will be dead within a year. Fatal Familial Insomnia attacks a specific region of the brain, destroying the ability to enter any sleep state. Victims hallucinate, lose motor control, then slip into a coma — all while technically conscious. Only around 100 families on Earth carry the gene. No drug stops it. No doctor has ever saved a patient. Would you want to know if you carried it?

candidates.topic: The Island That Belongs to No Country — Bir Tawil
candidates.teaser: There is a piece of land on Earth that every neighboring country is desperately trying NOT to own.
candidates.video_title: The Land Nobody on Earth Wants to Own
candidates.video_description: Bir Tawil is a 2,060 square kilometer territory between Egypt and Sudan that both countries actively refuse to claim. The bizarre reason comes down to a border dispute where owning Bir Tawil means giving up a much larger, more valuable region nearby.
candidates.script: There is a piece of land the size of a small country that literally no government on Earth wants to own. Bir Tawil sits between Egypt and Sudan — 2,060 square kilometers of territory both nations are legally refusing to claim. Why? Because whichever country claims it must give up rights to a far larger, fertile region nearby. So it sits there — ownerless, governmentless, the only land on Earth actively abandoned by its neighbors. Several private citizens have already tried to declare it their own kingdom.

candidates.teaser: The world's smartest codebreakers have spent over a century on one book — and still have no idea what it says.
candidates.video_title: 600 Years. 250 Pages. Nobody Can Read It.
candidates.video_description: The Voynich Manuscript is a 600-year-old illustrated book written in an entirely unknown script that no linguist, cryptographer, or AI system has ever successfully decoded. Carbon-dated to the early 15th century, it contains detailed illustrations of unknown plants and astronomical diagrams alongside its mysterious text.
candidates.script: The world's top codebreakers — including World War II cryptographers and modern AI — have all failed to read the same book. The Voynich Manuscript is 250 pages of dense, flowing script written in a language or code that has never been cracked. Carbon-dated to the early 1400s, it's filled with drawings of plants that don't exist and star charts that match nothing we know. Some experts now believe it may be a perfectly constructed hoax. Others think it holds real knowledge we simply lost.

candidates.teaser: Two people can share 100% of their DNA — yet still have something the universe will never duplicate for either of them.
candidates.video_title: Twins Share Every Gene — But Not This
candidates.video_description: Identical twins share the exact same DNA sequence, yet their fingerprints are always different. The pattern forms not from genetics but from the random physical pressure, position, and amniotic fluid turbulence each fetus experiences in the womb — making every print a one-time accident of physics.
candidates.script: Two people can share every single strand of DNA and still have fingerprints that look nothing alike. Identical twins are genetically perfect copies — same genes, same blueprint — but fingerprints aren't built by genes. They form from random turbulence in the womb: fluid pressure, the exact position of each fetus, tiny friction forces against the uterine wall during weeks six through thirteen. It's pure physics, never repeating. So your fingerprint isn't really about biology — it's a frozen accident of movement that happened before you were born.

candidates.topic: The Darkness That Has a Smell — Petrichor
candidates.teaser: That smell after it rains? Scientists know exactly what it is — and the answer is far stranger than you'd expect.
candidates.video_title: That Smell After Rain Has a Shocking Origin
candidates.video_description: Petrichor, the distinctive earthy scent after rainfall, is produced by a chemical called geosmin released by soil bacteria when raindrops strike the ground. Humans can detect geosmin at concentrations as low as 5 parts per trillion — a sensitivity 200,000 times sharper than sharks' ability to detect blood.
candidates.script: That smell after rain hits dry earth isn't rain at all — it's bacteria screaming. Soil microbes called Streptomyces release a chemical named geosmin the moment a raindrop strikes the ground. Humans can detect it at just 5 parts per trillion — a sensitivity 200,000 times sharper than a shark detecting blood. Scientists believe we evolved this ability because ancient humans desperately needed to find water sources to survive. So when that smell triggers something deep in you — that's millions of years of survival instinct firing at once.
